## Pull request overview

This PR completes implementation of all ObjectStack-spec field types in the `@object-ui/fields` package, wires them into the runtime/registry, and adds comprehensive documentation and examples covering all 26 field types. It also fixes the CSS export/import path so field widgets pick up component styles correctly and ensures the docs site loads and registers the new fields.

**Changes:**
- Implemented 14 new field widgets (DateTime, Time, Percent, Password, File, Image, Location, Formula, Summary, AutoNumber, User, Object, Vector, Grid) and registered them in both the component registry and field cell renderer mapping.
- Added a shared wrapper layer so all field widgets can be rendered via `ComponentDemo` for documentation, along with a full-field example schema and FIELD_TYPES overview docs.
- Fixed CSS and dependency wiring (`@object-ui/fields` export, CSS side effects, app provider registration) so the docs app and downstream consumers can use the fields package with correct styling.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 38 out of 39 changed files in this pull request and generated 14 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Updates lockfile to add the `@object-ui/fields` workspace dependency and platform metadata consistent with the new package usage. |
| packages/fields/vite.config.ts | Adds a `@` alias for `./src` to align with other packages and simplify imports when building the fields library. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/VectorField.tsx | Introduces a read-only vector/embedding viewer that previews the first few components and displays total dimensionality. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/UserField.tsx | Adds a user/owner field widget that renders selected users as avatars/badges and supports multi-select with removal. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/TimeField.tsx | Implements a time-only input widget using `<input type="time">` with simple read-only formatting. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/SummaryField.tsx | Adds a read-only summary/rollup widget that formats counts and numeric aggregates (sum/avg/min/max) with tabular numeric styling. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/SelectField.tsx | Adjusts `SelectField` to use `position="popper"` for correct dropdown positioning in the docs and host app. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/PercentField.tsx | Implements a percent widget that stores values as 0–1 decimals and displays them as 0–100 with configurable precision. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/PasswordField.tsx | Adds a password input widget with a show/hide toggle button, wired to the shared field props. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/ObjectField.tsx | Introduces an object/JSON editor widget using a textarea that parses JSON and shows pretty-printed read-only output. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/LocationField.tsx | Adds a location field widget that binds `{ latitude, longitude }` objects to a `\"lat, lng\"` text input. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/ImageField.tsx | Implements an image upload widget with previews, multiple-selection support, and remove controls. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx | Adds a grid/sub-table widget that summarizes row count in read-only mode and shows a small tabular preview otherwise. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/FormulaField.tsx | Adds a read-only formula widget that formats results differently based on the configured `return_type`. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/FileField.tsx | Implements a generic file upload widget that manages a list of uploaded files with metadata display and removal. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/DateTimeField.tsx | Adds a combined date/time widget based on `<input type=\"datetime-local\">` with localized read-only rendering. |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/AutoNumberField.tsx | Adds an auto-number field widget that displays generated identifiers in a monospace style. |
| packages/fields/src/index.tsx | Wires in CSS, defines cell renderers and mapping utilities, introduces the `createFieldRenderer` wrapper, registers all 26 field types (plus `field:`-prefixed variants) with `ComponentRegistry`, and re-exports all widgets. |
| packages/fields/src/index.css | Imports `@object-ui/components/style.css` so field widgets inherit all Shadcn/Tailwind styles from the components package. |
| packages/fields/package.json | Marks the package as having side effects and adds a `./style.css` export that points at the built CSS, enabling correct style consumption by bundlers. |
| examples/field-types-example.ts | Provides a comprehensive example `ObjectSchemaMetadata` illustrating configuration for all field types defined by the ObjectStack spec. |
| examples/FIELD_TYPES.md | Documents each field category, mapping types to widgets and describing behavior/features, and points to the example schema and spec file. |
| content/docs/fields/vector.mdx | Adds end-user documentation and examples for the VectorField, including schema details and AI/ML–oriented usage patterns. |
| content/docs/fields/user.mdx | Documents the User/Owner field semantics, schema, and backend integration patterns for ownership/assignment. |
| content/docs/fields/time.mdx | Introduces documentation and usage examples for the new Time field type. |
| content/docs/fields/summary.mdx | Documents the Summary/Rollup field type, including supported aggregation modes and backend aggregation patterns. |
| content/docs/fields/percent.mdx | Adds docs for the Percent field, explaining the 0–1 storage vs 0–100 display convention and configuration. |
| content/docs/fields/password.mdx | Provides docs and usage examples for the Password field, covering validation and security considerations. |
| content/docs/fields/object.mdx | Documents the Object field, its schema options, and backend validation patterns for JSON data. |
| content/docs/fields/meta.json | Extends the fields docs metadata to include all new field doc pages so they appear in the docs navigation. |
| content/docs/fields/location.mdx | Adds docs for the Location field, including schema, coordinate format, and typical geo use cases. |
| content/docs/fields/image.mdx | Documents the Image field widget, describing multiple uploads, previews, and typical constraints. |
| content/docs/fields/grid.mdx | Adds Grid field documentation, differentiating the basic inline grid field from the more advanced grid plugin. |
| content/docs/fields/formula.mdx | Provides docs for the Formula field type, including return-type handling and backend evaluation patterns. |
| content/docs/fields/file.mdx | Documents the File field widget’s schema, accepted MIME types, and integration considerations. |
| content/docs/fields/datetime.mdx | Adds documentation and examples for the DateTime field type. |
| content/docs/fields/auto-number.mdx | Documents the AutoNumber field, including formatting templates and backend sequence management patterns. |
| apps/site/package.json | Adds `@object-ui/fields` as a workspace dependency for the docs/site application. |
| apps/site/app/components/ObjectUIProvider.tsx | Ensures `registerFields()` is called alongside `initializeComponents()` so all field widgets are registered in the docs app runtime. |
</details>

[Show more details](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/security/code-scanning/129)

The remove button in `UserField` is icon-only and lacks an accessible label, which makes its purpose unclear to screen readers and assistive technologies. Align this with the pattern in `LookupField` by adding an `aria-label` that includes the user's display name (e.g., `Remove {name}`) so the control is accessible.

The remove button for each file is icon-only and has no `aria-label`, so screen readers will not announce its purpose. To improve accessibility, add an appropriate `aria-label` (for example, including the file name) so that users relying on assistive tech can understand and operate the control.
```suggestion
                  className="h-6 w-6 p-0"
                  aria-label={`Remove ${file.name || file.original_name || 'file'}`}
```

This table lists `ObjectField` as providing "Textarea with JSON validation, syntax highlighting", but the current `ObjectField` widget is a plain textarea without syntax highlighting and with only basic JSON parsing (no visible error feedback). To avoid confusing users, consider either enhancing the component to match this feature set or revising the description to match the current behavior.
```suggestion
- **Features**: Plain textarea with basic JSON validation (no syntax highlighting)
```

The GridField implementation does not respect the `readonly` flag as described: when `readonly` is true it only renders a simple "X rows" summary instead of the tabular view, while the non-readonly branch renders the full table even though there is no editing support here. This makes the runtime behavior inconsistent with the documented "Read-Only Grid" examples and the comment in this file that describes a simplified table view; consider always using the table view for the field widget (with editing delegated to the grid plugin) or aligning the documentation to the actual behavior.
```suggestion

```

`FileField` creates object URLs via `URL.createObjectURL(file)` for previews but never revokes them, which can lead to memory leaks when users repeatedly upload or replace files in a long-lived session. Consider tracking the created URLs and calling `URL.revokeObjectURL` when files are removed or when the component unmounts, similar to how `data-table.tsx` handles export URLs.

`ImageField` creates preview URLs with `URL.createObjectURL(file)` but never calls `URL.revokeObjectURL`, so repeated uploads can leak memory in long-running sessions. Please add cleanup (e.g., revoking URLs when images are removed or on unmount) to match the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase when creating object URLs.

The remove button over each image thumbnail is icon-only and lacks an `aria-label`, which makes it difficult for screen reader users to understand that it removes that specific image. Please add an accessible label (e.g., `aria-label={"Remove " + (img.name || `Image ${idx + 1}`)}`) so the control is clearly announced by assistive technologies.
```suggestion
                  className="absolute top-1 right-1 h-6 w-6 p-0 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity"
                  aria-label={`Remove ${img.name || `Image ${idx + 1}`}`}
```

The password visibility toggle button is removed from the tab order (`tabIndex={-1}`) and has no accessible label, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reliably discover or activate it. For better accessibility, keep the button focusable and add an `aria-label` that describes the current action (e.g., "Show password" / "Hide password").
